service_boundary: Represents the Amazon Bedrock inference platform, not Amazon's model families, SageMaker-hosted endpoints, Amazon Q, or Bedrock AgentCore.
regional_controls: Model, feature, and endpoint availability is region-specific. Inference profiles can route within a geography or globally, while single-region use and provisioned capacity have separate support matrices.
retention_controls: Data handling depends on the selected model, Bedrock feature, region, AWS account controls, and any applicable third-party model terms; cross-region profiles can change the processing locations involved.
routing: Bedrock inference profiles can route a selected model across supported AWS regions; this is regional capacity routing rather than arbitrary cross-model selection.
customization: Eligible base models can be customized, and imported or custom models use distinct identifiers and capacity requirements.
strengths: One AWS control plane covers models from several publishers, regional IAM boundaries, and multiple capacity modes.
Inference profiles and provisioned throughput support production capacity and residency choices.
tradeoffs: Availability and API compatibility vary by model, endpoint, feature, and AWS region.
Third-party models can add publisher-specific terms on top of the AWS agreement.

response_integrity.note: Scoped to reasoning-text blocks. The API reference states the `signature` field on a ReasoningTextBlock is "A token that verifies that the reasoning text was generated by the model." Ordinary tool-call and message content carries no such field.
response_integrity.scope: Amazon Bedrock API reference, ReasoningTextBlock, for Amazon Bedrock

upstream_disclosure.note: The data-protection guide states: "Because the model providers don't have access to those accounts, they don't have access to Amazon Bedrock logs or to customer prompts and completions." Third-party model providers are explicitly denied access to plaintext.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Amazon Bedrock data-protection guide, for Amazon Bedrock

credential_handling.note: The service offers no customer-supplied upstream-key path: "You must be authenticated as the AWS account root user, an IAM user, or by assuming an IAM role."
credential_handling.scope: Amazon Bedrock security and identity guide, for Amazon Bedrock

cache_isolation.note: The prompt-caching guide describes the feature, its pricing, and cache lifetime but never states whether a cache entry is scoped to the requesting account.
cache_isolation.scope: Amazon Bedrock prompt-caching guide, for Amazon Bedrock

vulnerability_disclosure.note: AWS publishes a vulnerability-reporting programme scoped to "AWS Services delivered by AWS and publicly available to customers. (e.g. Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS)." Bedrock is such a service though not named individually.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: AWS vulnerability-reporting programme, for Amazon Bedrock

independent_audit.note: The AWS SOC services-in-scope page names the service directly: "Amazon Bedrock [excludes Amazon Bedrock Marketplace]" is listed with a checkmark under SOC 1, 2, 3 in scope, dated "Last updated: August 11, 2026".
independent_audit.scope: AWS SOC services-in-scope page, for Amazon Bedrock

resolved.summary: Bedrock has since documented a prompt-caching feature; the paper found no caching detectable at the time of its 2024 audit, so this is not a finding of unsafe sharing.
